title: Cultural and multicultural topics in neuropsychology journal titles from 2021-2024: A follow-up study to data from 2010-2020.
abstract: Cultural influences on brain function were recognized by early leaders in the field of neuropsychology. In articles from 13 neuropsychology journals published from 2010-2020, cultural or multicultural content was reflected in 6.2% of the titles (Ready et al., 2025). To update these data, the current study determined the cultural or multicultural content in titles from the same journals published in 2021-2024.Titles from articles published in 13 neuropsychology journals from 2021-2024 were collected and coded for cultural and multicultural content. The study aimed to (1) determine if cultural or multicultural content increased from 2010-2020 to 2021-2024 and (2) explore topics that were most and least likely to appear in publications pertaining to cultural or multicultural issues.Cultural or multicultural neuropsychology content was coded in 14.8% of all titles in neuropsychology journals from 2021-2024 (range 2.7% to 21.3%), which is an increase from 6.2% in 2010-2020 (range 1.1% to 13.4%). Normative data and psychometric topics were addressed significantly (< .05) more often in cultural/multicultural titles versus non-cultural/multicultural titles, whereas psychiatric, medical, and neurologic issues were addressed significantly less often. There were no significant correlations between year of publication and cultural/multicultural titles ( = -0.09) or between impact factor and cultural/multicultural titles ( = -0.24).The field of clinical neuropsychology is publishing more scholarship about cultural and multicultural topics in 2021-2024 than in 2010-2020. More research on how cultural issues interface with psychiatric, medical, and neurologic issues in a neuropsychological context are fruitful avenues for future research.
